text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- President Jorge Sampaio refused a visit to the Vatican that was scheduled for May 27. Sampaio's decision was a protest against the protocol surrounding the visit. Sampaio's divorce from his first wife means that he could not be received by Pope John Paul II in the presence of his second wife Maria Jose Ritta who would have to wait in an anti-room and be received separately by the Pope.
- Saudi Aramco will buy a 27.5 percent stake in state oil company Petrogal-Petroleos de Portugal.

- According to a poll by the newspaper, the ruling Socialist Party has 39 percent of voters' support -- four percentage points more than a month ago -- while the opposition centre-right Social Democrats have 31 percent support.
- Oil company Petrogal has decided to lower gas prices for industry and restaurants by 12 percent after July 1, to prevent loss of market share to natural gas, a company spokesman said.

- The bank Montepio Geral, via the purchase of insurance company Seguros Lusitania, will be the biggest shareholder in insurance company O Trabalho, holding 40 percent of its capital, a source linked to the deal said.
- Investment funds BCI Accoes Portugal and Caixagest Accoes Portugal are the market leaders.
- Philips will open two new factories in Portugal by the end of the year, creating 300 jobs. One factory will produce batteries and the other television components.
